cues.text: How many of you read the headline, skip the article, and go straight to the comments?
Before we even open the link, likes, upvotes and top comments have already shaped our opinion.
If it's about burgers, who cares if a million people liked it?
But when it affects your friends and your family, public perception matters most.
Candor doesn't ban bots or flag accounts. It shows how narratives behave, and what kinds of accounts support them.
Paste any public Reddit thread, and Candor analyzes it live.
Or browse threads we've already analyzed.
Each one shows its narrative distribution, an AI summary, and how many commenters were flagged.
Stage 1 · context.dev pulls posts, comments and profiles in real time.
Every engaged commenter is scored from zero to one hundred, on five weighted criteria.
Is this an established, real person? Did they write it? Are they acting in concert with others? Did they earn their upvotes? And do they do this elsewhere?
Click any badge to see the evidence.
Stage 2 · Gemini embeddings turn each comment into a vector; HDBSCAN finds dense clusters of shared meaning.
NVIDIA Nemotron names each cluster and explains it. That's the narrative.
Raise the filter to fold away low-scoring accounts, and see what the real people are saying.
The dashboard scales this up: 4,453 posts and comments, grouped into narratives and topics.
Every topic carries its own authenticity score.
Narrative weather replays the conversation over time, so you can watch narratives swell as they go viral.
It's not a verdict on any person. It's the crowd behind each narrative, on transparent criteria.
We can't fix the crowd. But we can show you who's in it.
See it for yourself. See it with Candor.
